newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate eases 40 bps to 11.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate eases 40 bps to 11.3 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average money market rate edged down 40 basis points to 11.3 percent despite strong demand on Tuesday as banks mostly made call money borrowings.

Dealers put daily trade at a meagre 24.2 million kuna against demand for 45 million. They said the banks' deposits had shrunk over the past few days and hinted central bank intervention may well be needed.
Fresh placements accounted for 20.7 million kuna of which 18.7 million were call money loans struck at a higher weighted rate of 11 percent, up 10 basis points from Monday.
Term loans remained unchanged ranging from 9.0 percent charged by insurers and interbank rates struck at 15 and 18 percent.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Wednesday firmer at 6.0868 against the dollar and at 3.5704 versus the German mark. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
